editorial:
Sydney Wells is a talented violinist who has been blind since childhood, and when she finally gets a cornea transplant, her world opens up in ways she never expected. Instead of just seeing her apartment and her sister Helen, she starts catching glimpses of shadowy figures and strange visions that no one else can see. The movie follows her as she tries to figure out whether she is losing her mind or if something supernatural is really happening. It has a creepy, slow-burn feel that keeps you guessing without relying on cheap jump scares every five minutes.

Jessica Alba carries the film well, and the story moves at a steady pace that builds tension nicely. The downside is that some scenes feel a bit predictable if you have seen other ghost movies, and a few moments drag in the middle. Still, it is a solid pick for fans of supernatural thrillers who want something atmospheric rather than gory. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final act, Sydney travels to Mexico and learns her donor was Ana Cristina Martinez, a woman who could foresee disasters. Sydney realizes the visions are warnings, not hauntings. On a train, she sees a deadly explosion coming and gets everyone off in time. The train explodes, and Sydney survives but loses her sight again. The visions stop, and she returns to her normal life, grateful but changed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves supernatural thrillers with a mystery at the center.
